inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,840 logical lines. The paper derives exact CUE characteristic-polynomial generating functions, turns their logarithms into cumulant and Fourier descriptions, proves Gaussian and asymptotically independent real/imaginary log-value laws, and calibrates matrix size against zeta-zero density. Its main zeta-facing mechanism separates a universal random-matrix factor from arithmetic prime factors, tests the finite-size model against Odlyzko data, and extends the same machinery to other circular symmetry classes. The prose is coherent, but many extracted displays lose symbols and require the PDF for exact formula reuse.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,234 logical lines. The paper constructs a unitary matrix model whose resolvent is built from the symmetric zeta function after conformally mapping the critical line to the unit circle. The resulting eigenvalue density has logarithmic spikes at mapped zeros, its couplings are Li coefficients, and a representation-theoretic large-N calculation relates eigenphases to Young-diagram row lengths to produce a free-fermion phase-space picture. Later prime-counting correspondences and the identification θ=πu(h) are explicitly heuristic. The text layer is readable, but several long displays and the physical interpretation require source-image verification and careful evidential labeling.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,045 logical lines. The paper randomizes the dilation parameters in the Nyman-Beurling criterion and distinguishes two approximation notions: pNB takes an expected squared random error, while gNB approximates using expected fractional-part functions. It proves pNB implies RH by extracting a deterministic witness on a positive-probability event, obtains a converse for variables tightly concentrated near deterministic dilations, and proves a gNB sufficient criterion for noncompact support when coefficient-weighted tails are controlled. A probabilistic identity identifies expected fractional parts with the Müntz transform, supplying the reverse implication for dilated laws. The extraction is generally coherent, with formula verification advisable for quantitative exponents and norms.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 717 logical lines. The paper studies Riemann's explicit density formula in the direction from zeros to primes and prime powers. It emphasizes the conditional ordering of the zero sum, uses Gaussian convolution to make line intensities comparable, derives an exponentially damped and absolutely convergent sum rule, and converts the damping threshold into a resolution/error law relating the largest known zero to the largest reliably reconstructed prime power. It also cleanly records two limits of the quantum-chaos analogy: moving zeros off the critical line preserves peak locations but corrupts weights, and the zero-indexed oscillations lack the repetition and amplitude structure of a dynamical trace formula. The extraction is coherent apart from routine display artifacts.
